summary: A cable manager for the same rack keyholes as the adaptor holder. A 20 x 54 x 4 plate carries the two teardrop rack pins (z 8 and 46) and, centred on each pin, a cable loop 40 wide and 12 long: a rounded U strap lid (2.4 wall, R6 outside) over a 35.2 x 12 cable space, hinged along the cable on a 3-knuckle hinge with 45 deg cone pins and closed by a skirt-and-barb latch, like the reference Deskcable organiser. Everything prints in place in one go, lying on its back (rack pin heads on the bed, lids on top, already on their hinges); the only support is under the plate's back. A 12 x 20 window saves material. PLA, one per plate.

assumptions: A1: one loop centred on each rack pin (user).
A2: loop 40 wide (user); cable space depth = reference + 2 mm (user).
A3: print in place on its back, like the reference (user, rev 4): the lids print on their hinges; only the plate's back needs support (build plate only).
A4: gaps (D19), barb (D27) and skirt (D26) are first guesses for PLA, checked by the motion sweep only; print one and adjust in 0.05 mm steps.
A5: the rack pins now print with their layers across them (they stood upright in the tested sample); fine for the light load of cables.
A6: the lid ceiling bridges about 28 mm over the cable space, as in the reference.
